blocks.text:
After breakfast, cross the Tancredo Neves Bridge for a guided visit to the Argentine side of Iguazu National Park.

Here, walkways stretch across the broad river, descend the slopes and lead you much closer to individual waterfalls. The contrast with the previous day’s panoramic views from Brazil is striking: yesterday the cascades formed one sweeping picture; today the route reveals them one by one.

The highlight is the Devil’s Throat. Walkways lead across the river to reach it. Even before you approach the observation deck, you can hear the powerful roar. At the edge, a white curtain of mist, spray and the continuous thunder of falling water surrounds you.

Return to your hotel after the tour.

The Argentine side offers more individual trails and closer views of the water. Walkways cross the broad river before approaching the rim of the falls. On one stretch, the water flows calmly between islands; moments later, it plunges over the edge almost beneath your feet. At the Devil’s Throat, a dense cloud of spray partly obscures the view, while the noise and vibration of the immense flow make themselves felt.
